units.1: General description of plain power looms, introduction to power loom weaving process, primary, secondary and auxiliary motion of plain power looms, types of sheds, tappet shedding, over and under pick motions, Beating-up Mechanism – Eccentricity of sley, Timing and Synchronization of Primary motion, Temple and its utility, Negative and positive take up motion, five wheel and seven wheel take up motion, positive & negative let-off motions. Contact hours required = 9
units.2: Scope & limitation of dobby, negative and positive dobby, right hand & left hand dobby & their pegging methods, Development in dobby, brief description of Cromption and Knowles dobby, cross border dobby, heald reversing motion. Warp protective mechanism- loose reed & fast reed, weft detection mechanisms- side and center weft fork motion. Contact hours required = 9
units.3: Types of jacquards and their principle of working, size and figuring capacity of jacquard, Single lift single cylinder Jacquard, Double lift single cylinder, Double lift double cylinder, split harness, cross border jacquards, Different system of harness tie- up, terry mechanism, Recent developments in jacquard weaving. Contact hours required = 9
units.4: Multiple box motion and their types, Pick-at will, pick and pick motion. Automatic loom: pirn change, shuttle change loom, detailed study of various motions of automatic looms, mechanical warp stop motions, electro-mechanical warp stop motion. Contact hours required = 9
units.5: Gear, pully & belt Calculations. Production and efficiency of machine e, take up and let off, Jacquard Design and Harness Calculations – Calculations related to Sett of harness, sett of warp, ends per repeat, size of repeat, number of repeats, symmetrical repeat setting for straight draft and pointed draft, number of cords per hook and casting out. Loom shed calculation – Efficiency, Production and Production Planning. Contact hours required = 8

units.1: Theories of colour measurement, Beer–Lambert’s law and Kubelka-Munk theory and their application in colour assessment and colour matching; whiteness and yellowness indices. Dyeing equilibrium; dye-fibre interaction; adsorption isotherm; dye affinity; heat of dyeing; half dyeing time Basic parameters of dyeing Viz. Percentage of shade, Percentage of exhaustion, percentage expression and effects of MLR. Contact hours required = 9
units.2: Basic characteristics of dyes and pigments; classification of dyes and principle of application of dyes; Principles and methods of application of Direct Dyes, reactive, vat, Solubilized vat, azoic with function of chemicals used and effect of process conditions on cellulosic fiber. Methods of dyeing of Wool and Silk with Acid, Chrome, Prematalized (1:1 & 1:2), and Reactive dyes with Process details such as time Temperature and pH, Effect of Electrolytes and use of leveling agents. units.3: Approaches for dyeing of polyester – Various methods of dyeing Polyester involving use of chemical and Thermal Energy (Carrier Dyeing and H.T.H.P. subjects.name_print: KHT 503 QUALITY EVALUATION OF FIBRES AND YARNS
subjects.marks_print: 3 1 0 | 30 20 44 | (PS blank) | 100 | (PE blank) | 150 | 4 (p.2 Sem-V scheme row 3; header columns CT TA Total PS TE PE | End Semester Total | Credit)

units.1: Selection of samples for quality assessment – random and biased samples – squaring technique and zoning technique for fibre selection; yarn sampling - use of random numbers - sampling for various types of yarn tests- yarn strength, linear density, elongation, twist. Contact hours required = 9
units.2: Fibre testing, the fibre quality index and spinnablity; Fibre length and length uniformity measuring techniques. Tensile Strength Testing modes – CRT, CRE and CRL; Fibre strength and its relation to yarn strength. Fiber bundle strength tests. Contact hours required = 8
units.3: Fibre fineness – definition- comparison of various fibres – its importance in yarn manufacture; measurement techniques. Cotton fibre maturity, estimation by microscopic method - maturity ratio and index, estimation by other methods – optical, air flow differential dyeing; its importance in spinning. Fibre trash – influence on quality; measurement – principle and estimation of micro-dust for rotor spinning. High volume instrument for total fiber quality measurement. Contact hours required = 9
units.4: Yarn Appearance and grading, yarn mass evenness parameters – measurement – electronic mass evenness determination – Yarn fault classification –Yarn abrasion resistance – importance and measuring technique. Yarn hairiness – importance and assessment techniques. Twist in single and ply yarns –twist direction – twist factor – twist and yarn strength; twist measurement and breaking twist angle measurement. Analysis of data and test reports such as HVI, AFIS, Classimat. Contact hours required = 9
units.5: Tensile characteristics –study of strength, single yarn strength; Lea count strength product (CSP) and Corrected Count Strength Product (CCSP), elongation, work of rupture, initial modulus, work factor and yield point – determination of yield point. Stress-strain relations of natural and manmade fibres, influence of fibre structure, humidity and temperature on tensile characteristics. Time effects Study of creep phenomena. Elastic recovery and its relation to stress and strain of fibres; mechanical conditioning of fibres and its influence on elastic recovery. Load cycling and extension cycling-their effect on elastic recovery. Introduction about torsional and flexural rigidity of fibers. Contact hours required = 9
